A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same pCQO-MIS work. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched across the title, layout and appendix changes.

before.justification: v4 reports original pCQO-MIS experiments on ER, SATLIB, GNM and DIMACS graphs, including benchmark results, scalability measurements and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendices C and E.

M1.justification: The stated QUBO-based checking rule changes from an adjacency coefficient of alpha*gamma_Q/2 in v4 Equation (11) to alpha*gamma_Q in v5 Equation (10), correcting the projected-gradient check. The clique-informed objective, parallel initializations and momentum-based optimization remain unchanged; the added gradient line in Algorithm 1 makes an existing calculation explicit.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ER, SATLIB, GNM and DIMACS coverage, including dense-graph scalability, varying-density ER tests and stationary-point examples. Appendix relocation introduces no new dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main benchmarks and corresponding appendix experiments: the same exact, heuristic, learning and sampling methods are retained, including ReduMIS for DIMACS, dNN-MIS in Table 4 and DIFUSCO in Table 5. The expanded PI-GNN discussion does not introduce an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The reported graph counts, evaluation metrics, time limits, hardware and tested hyperparameters remain unchanged. v5 adds tuning and runtime-accounting disclosures for existing experiments, without reporting revised experimental settings or reruns.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the MC-term ablation, checking-runtime comparison, stationary-point analysis, density-shift evaluation, parameter sweeps and batch-count results. The expanded parameter discussion adds qualifications, not new analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same averaging over graph collections. Neither adds or removes repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–10 match. Examples include Table 1's pCQO-MIS averages of 425.148 on SATLIB and 45.109 on ER, and the DIMACS finding of 49 versus ReduMIS's 58 optimal solutions among 61 graphs. Matched figures retain their results; Figure 5's changed dimensions do not change its bar values.

T1.justification: v5 revises Definition 3 and the main theorem statements from MIS to MaxIS vectors, aligning them with the maximal-set statements already present in v4 Appendix A. It also corrects the QUBO checking expression and explicitly conditions the squared-L1 identity on nonnegative coordinates. The detailed proof arguments and parameter bounds are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about the clique-informed formulation, local minimizers, stationary points, parallel optimization, efficient checking and comparative performance. The new title and Impact Statement reframe or repeat existing contributions.

C2.justification: v4 Appendix D.5 broadly describes low parameter sensitivity. v5 Appendix E.5 limits this interpretation to obtaining feasible solutions and acknowledges that tuning is needed for the best ER and SATLIB results. Table 1 also newly qualifies the runtime comparison by stating that pCQO tuning time is excluded.

D1.justification: v5 explicitly describes grid-search tuning, discloses that DIMACS parameters were optimized on one graph and reused across the dataset, and states that reported pCQO runtimes exclude tuning. It replaces the anonymous code-hosting link with a GitHub repository link. These are documentation and access-reference changes, not evidence of changed experiments.

R1.justification: The dataless-method discussion expands from v4's short Ichikawa description to explicitly discuss Schuetz et al.'s PI-GNN, its d-regular evaluation coverage and subsequent work including Ichikawa. The bibliography also adds Langley (2000). The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The main section sequence remains intact, with localized paragraph rewrites, terminology corrections, a new title and an added Impact Statement. Main-text proof sketches are removed while full appendix proofs remain, and the neural-network interpretation moves from Section 3.1 to Appendix B.

P2.justification: The single-column manuscript becomes an ICML-style document with a two-column main text, running headers and extensively reflowed displays. v4 Figure 2 moves to Appendix B as v5 Figure 3, while the scalability plot becomes Figure 2. Figure 5 is redrawn with a shorter aspect ratio, horizontal category labels and fewer vertical-axis ticks.

improvement.justification: v5 provides a modest improvement through the corrected QUBO checking formula, better alignment of main-text MaxIS statements with the appendix, and clearer disclosure of tuning requirements and excluded tuning costs. These improve consistency and experimental transparency while preserving the evidence and full proofs. The remaining statement that MIS and MaxIS are used interchangeably leaves some terminology ambiguity.
